title: Ambiguous loss and the “myth of closure,” with Pauline Boss, PhD

sentences.en: It's been two years since the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a global pandemic.
sentences.zh: 自世界卫生组织宣布新冠肺炎为全球大流行以来，已经过去两年了。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's hard to believe it's been that long, while on other days it feels even longer.
sentences.zh: 有时很难相信已经过去了这么久，而在其他日子里，感觉时间过得更漫长。

sentences.en: Nearly everyone has lost something over these past two years.
sentences.zh: 在过去这两年里，几乎每个人都失去了一些东西。

sentences.en: Many losses were tragic, especially the deaths of loved ones from COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 许多失去是悲惨的，尤其是因新冠肺炎失去挚亲。

sentences.en: But even the smaller losses have added up.
sentences.zh: 但即使是那些较小的失去，也在不断累积。

sentences.en: Graduations, birthday parties, and weddings that were rescheduled and rescheduled again and finally canceled.
sentences.zh: 毕业典礼、生日派对和婚礼一改再改，最终被迫取消。

sentences.en: Friends and acquaintances whom you can't see or who have fallen out of touch.
sentences.zh: 那些无法见面或已经失去联系的朋友和熟人。

sentences.en: People who have lost jobs and businesses and maybe even their confidence in the future.
sentences.zh: 失去了工作和企业的人，甚至可能失去了对未来的信心。

sentences.en: Now, after two years, and with, we hope, the latest variant receding, many people are hoping yet again to close the book on COVID and move on with regular life.
sentences.zh: 现在，两年过去了，随着我们所希望的最新变异株逐渐消退，许多人再次期盼着彻底翻过新冠这一页，回归正常生活。

sentences.en: But what if closing the book is an elusive goal?
sentences.zh: 但如果“翻过这一页”是一个难以企及的目标呢？

sentences.en: What if closure is not what we should be aiming for?
sentences.zh: 如果“释怀”根本不应该是我们的目标呢？

sentences.en: And instead, there's a different way to think about life after loss.
sentences.zh: 相反，对于失去后的生活，其实有另一种思考方式。

sentences.en: What have we learned about grief and resilience and moving on after two years of pandemic life?
sentences.zh: 经历了两年疫情生活后，我们对悲伤、韧性以及如何继续生活有了哪些了解？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学聊天室》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Pauline Boss, a professor emerita in the Department of Family Social Service at the University of Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是明尼苏达大学家庭社会服务系的荣休教授保琳·博斯博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Boss coined the term ambiguous loss in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 博斯博士在20世纪70年代提出了“模棱两可的失去”这一概念。

sentences.en: Coming from the discipline of family therapy, she originally implied the term to families mourning a loved one whose loss was in some way unresolved, like a soldier missing in war.
sentences.zh: 出于家庭治疗领域的背景，她最初将这个词应用于那些哀悼亲人的家庭，这些亲人的失去在某种程度上并未得到解决，比如战争中失踪的士兵。

sentences.en: In the years since, she and other researchers have expanded the scope of ambiguous loss, using
sentences.zh: 在此后的几年里，她和其他研究人员扩大了“模棱两可的失去”的范围，将其作为

sentences.en: it as a framework through which to view any number of personal, communal, or global losses, from the pandemic to racial trauma to climate change.
sentences.zh: 一个观察各种个人、社群或全球失去的框架，从大流行到种族创伤再到气候变化。

sentences.en: Her new book, The Myth of Closure, Ambiguous Loss in a Time of Pandemic and Change, addresses these topics and more.
sentences.zh: 她的新书《释怀的神话：大流行与变革时期的模棱两可的失去》探讨了这些话题以及更多内容。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Boss.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您作客我们的节目，博斯博士。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Let's start with the title of your book, The Myth of Closure.
sentences.zh: 让我们从您的书名《释怀的神话》开始谈起。

sentences.en: Many of us tend to think that we want closure after a death or a divorce or a breakup.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人往往认为，在经历亲人离世、离婚或分手后，我们需要一个了结或释怀。

sentences.en: Why do you believe that closure is the wrong thing to be looking for after we lose something or someone?
sentences.zh: 为什么您认为在失去某人或某物后，寻找释怀是错误的方向？

sentences.en: Well, closure has a definition meaning finality.
sentences.zh: 嗯，“释怀”的定义意味着终结。

sentences.en: It means closing the door on something that has happened.
sentences.zh: 这意味着对已经发生的事情关上大门。

sentences.en: It's a perfectly good word in the business community for closing a contract, for closing a real estate deal, or for closing a road after a flood has occurred.
sentences.zh: 在商业领域，它是一个很好的词，用来指关闭一份合同、完成一笔房地产交易，或者在发生洪水后封闭一条道路。

sentences.en: But it is a harmful word in human relationships.
sentences.zh: 但在人际关系中，它却是一个有害的词。

sentences.en: It indicates that even though we have had attachment to someone or something, like a pet, that once they are gone, we can close the door on that.
sentences.zh: 它暗示了尽管我们曾经对某人或某物（比如宠物）产生过依恋，但一旦他们离去，我们就可以为此关上大门。

sentences.en: That's not true.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: There are continuing bonds, as has been now declared in the grief literature, and that we don't close the door.
sentences.zh: 正如悲伤文学中所阐述的那样，情感纽带会持续存在，我们并没有关上大门。

sentences.en: We live with loss and grief.
sentences.zh: 我们带着失去与悲伤共同生活。

sentences.en: Do you think this desire for closure is culture-specific?
sentences.zh: 您认为这种对释怀的渴望是特定文化独有的吗？

sentences.en: Is it something that Americans are particularly invested in, or is it even a more universal desire?
sentences.zh: 这是美国人特别执着的东西，还是一种更具普遍性的渴望？

sentences.en: It's not a universal desire.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种普遍的渴望。

sentences.en: It is, I think, more American than anywhere else, perhaps because we're a very mastery-oriented culture.
sentences.zh: 我认为它在美国比在其他任何地方都更为明显，也许是因为我们是一个非常崇尚掌控力的文化。

sentences.en: We believe in fixing things, finding cures.
sentences.zh: 我们坚信能够解决问题、找到治疗方法。

sentences.en: We do that very well, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们在这方面做得很好。

sentences.en: And we have put people in outer space and helicopters on Mars and a camera into deep space.
sentences.zh: 我们将人类送上了太空，把直升机开上了火星，还将相机送入了深空。

sentences.en: We are really good at solving problems and precision and fixing things.
sentences.zh: 我们在解决问题、精确度和修复事物方面真的很擅长。

sentences.en: But now and then something happens in human relationships that can't be fixed.
sentences.zh: 但偶尔在人际关系中会发生一些无法修复的事情。

sentences.en: A terminal illness, or in this case, a pandemic that at first we didn't understand.
sentences.zh: 绝症，或者在这个案例中，是一场起初我们并不了解的大流行。

sentences.en: We couldn't master this enemy that was unseen, the virus.
sentences.zh: 我们无法掌控这个看不见的敌人——病毒。

sentences.en: Eventually, by the way, the scientists did master it, which was wonderful.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，科学家们最终确实掌控了它，这太棒了。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, that virus still lurks out there somewhere, can't be seen, very ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 然而，那个病毒仍然潜伏在某个地方，看不见摸不着，非常含糊不清。

sentences.en: It's an ambiguous enemy that is still with us.
sentences.zh: 它是一个至今仍伴随着我们的模棱两可的敌人。

sentences.en: And even when the pandemic is over, it apparently will turn into an endemic, which means the virus
sentences.zh: 而且即使在大流行结束后，它显然也会变成一种地方性流行病，这意味着病毒

sentences.en: will still be here, as is the virus of 1918, only we just have an annual flu shot for that.
sentences.zh: 仍将存在，就像1918年的流感病毒一样，只是我们现在每年都要打流感疫苗。

sentences.en: So if not closure, you talked about living with the loss.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果不谈释怀，您刚才谈到了与失去共存。

sentences.en: How do people do that?
sentences.zh: 人们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: What's different about saying it's over and done with and saying, this is still with me?
sentences.zh: 说“事情已经结束了”与说“这仍然伴随着我”，两者有什么区别？

sentences.en: Well, the difference is that what people really want is finality, is clarity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，区别在于人们真正想要的是终结，是清晰明确。

sentences.en: What they really want is certainty about what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他们真正想要的是对正在发生的事情有确定感。

sentences.en: I understand that totally.
sentences.zh: 我完全理解这一点。

sentences.en: We have a little more certainty now about the pandemic than we had before, thanks to the scientists
sentences.zh: 多亏了那些一路摸索前行并顺便在前人研究基础上不断推进的科学家和医务工作者

sentences.en: and the medical people who have learned along the way and who built on previous research, by the way.
sentences.zh: ，我们现在对这场大流行的确定感比以前多了一些。

sentences.en: And so what human beings want is not closure after a loss.
sentences.zh: 因此，人类在经历失去后想要的并不是释怀。

sentences.en: What they want is certainty of what that loss was, if it's a human loss or even a pet loss, where the remains are, and that they're not just missing in action.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是确定那种失去到底是什么，如果那是失去亲人或宠物，遗体在哪里，他们是否不仅仅是失踪。

sentences.en: That ambiguity is very, very stressful on top of a loss.
sentences.zh: 这种含糊不清在失去之上带来了非常非常大的压力。

sentences.en: In other words, it exaggerates the pain of the loss.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它夸大了失去带来的痛苦。

sentences.en: It freezes the grief, and it freezes the family processes, the couple and family processes that could go on.
sentences.zh: 它冻结了悲伤，也冻结了本可以继续进行的家庭流程，包括伴侣和家庭之间的互动流程。

sentences.en: No decision-making happens.
sentences.zh: 没有任何决策能够做出。

sentences.en: People wait.
sentences.zh: 人们在等待。

sentences.en: And of course, sometimes they wait for decades, which is not functional in families and couples.
sentences.zh: 当然，有时他们一等就是几十年，这在家庭和伴侣关系中是无法正常运转的。

sentences.en: The family and couple system has to move on without the missing person.
sentences.zh: 家庭和伴侣系统必须在没有失踪人员的情况下继续生活下去。

sentences.en: And so I recommend both-hand thinking, whereby they both hope for a good outcome, either finding remains or having the person return.
sentences.zh: 因此，我建议采取“双向思维”，即他们既盼望有一个好的结果，比如找到遗体或亲人归来。

sentences.en: They hope for certainty.
sentences.zh: 他们渴望确定性。

sentences.en: But they also move forward with their daily lives.
sentences.zh: 但他们同时也带着日常生活继续向前迈进。

sentences.en: It has to be both.
sentences.zh: 必须两者兼顾。

sentences.en: It can't be one or the other.
sentences.zh: 不能非此即彼。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the term ambiguous loss, which you coined in the 1970s, in the context of family therapy.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们来谈谈您在20世纪70年代在家庭治疗背景下提出的“模棱两可的失去”这一概念。

sentences.en: And you define two different types of ambiguous loss.
sentences.zh: 您定义了两种不同类型的模棱两可的失去。

sentences.en: Loss in which a loved one is missing physically, and loss in which a loved one is missing psychologically.
sentences.zh: 一种是亲人身体上失踪的失去，另一种是亲人心理上失踪的失去。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that early work and what led you to study this phenomenon?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈那段早期的工作以及是什么促使您研究这种现象吗？

sentences.en: Well, what led me to study this phenomenon is that when I was studying for my doctorate at
sentences.zh: 嗯，促使我研究这种现象的原因是，当我在威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校攻读博士学位时，

sentences.en: the University of Wisconsin in Madison, I was observing Dr. Carl Whitaker in the Department of Psychiatry, who was teaching family therapy at the time.
sentences.zh: 我正在观察精神病学系的卡尔·惠特克博士，他当时正在教授家庭治疗。

sentences.en: And families would come in with the child as the identified patient.
sentences.zh: 家庭会带着被确诊为患者的孩子来看病。

sentences.en: What I noticed was that the fathers were always angry at being there.
sentences.zh: 我注意到的是，父亲们总是对来到这里感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Know that this was the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 要知道那是20世纪70年代。

sentences.en: And the fathers would say, why am I here?
sentences.zh: 父亲们会说，我为什么会在这里？

sentences.en: I should be at my job.
sentences.zh: 我应该去上班。

sentences.en: The children are mother's business.
sentences.zh: 孩子是母亲的事。

sentences.en: And so I wrote a paper as a grad student about the psychological absence of the fathers in an intact family.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为一名研究生，我写了一篇关于完整家庭中父亲心理缺席的论文。

sentences.en: So I was about to study psychological father absence in an intact family.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时准备研究完整家庭中父亲的心理缺席。

sentences.en: That was my first publication.
sentences.zh: 那是我的第一篇出版物。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, I was studying over in sociology, a theory of construction.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我在社会学系学习建构理论。

sentences.en: And the professor said, that's a good term, psychological absence.
sentences.zh: 教授说，这是个好词，心理缺席。

sentences.en: But it's about more than fathers, Pauline.
sentences.zh: 但保琳，这不仅仅关乎父亲。

sentences.en: He said, think about a more general term.
sentences.zh: 他说，想想一个更广义的词。

sentences.en: And so I went home and pondered about it a long time, but eventually came up with the term ambiguous loss.
sentences.zh: 于是我回家琢磨了很久，最终想出了“模棱两可的失去”这个词。

sentences.en: So it could be anyone in the family.
sentences.zh: 所以它可以指家庭中的任何成员。

sentences.en: I was studying families at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在研究家庭。

sentences.en: And so I had it at that level that a person could either be physically missing.
sentences.zh: 因此我在那个层面上认识到，一个人可能在身体上失踪。

sentences.en: An extreme example would be soldiers missing in war, loved ones kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 极端的例子是战争中失踪的士兵、被绑架的亲人。

sentences.en: A more common example comes from divorce and adoption and so on.
sentences.zh: 更常见的例子来自离婚、收养等等。

sentences.en: Or the person could be psychologically absent.
sentences.zh: 或者这个人可能在心理上缺席。

sentences.en: And the most common use of that now is for caregivers who are taking care of a loved one who has dementia, Alzheimer's disease, or the over 80 other kinds of conditions that cause
sentences.zh: 现在最常将其用于照顾患有痴呆症、阿尔茨海默病或导致痴呆的其他80多种疾病的亲人的照顾者。

sentences.en: dementia.
sentences.zh: 痴呆症。

sentences.en: But it also could be used for a traumatic brain injury.
sentences.zh: 但它也可以用于创伤性脑损伤。

sentences.en: It could be used for severe depression and other severe mental illnesses.
sentences.zh: 它可以用于严重抑郁症和其他严重精神疾病。

sentences.en: More common examples of psychological ambiguous loss would be preoccupation with work so that you're not available to your family or your partner.
sentences.zh: 心理上模棱两可的失去的更常见例子是对工作的全神贯注，导致你无法陪伴家人或伴侣。

sentences.en: Or it could be the preoccupation with our devices so that, you know, you see a couple at a restaurant having a lovely dinner together and both have their heads in their telephones.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是对电子设备的沉迷，比如你在餐馆里看到一对伴侣在一起愉快地吃晚餐，而两人的头都埋在手机里。

sentences.en: So that's a more common problem right now, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是目前更常见的问题。

sentences.en: So that's how it all got started.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样开始的。

sentences.en: And then more recently in the new book, I have raised the ambiguous loss theory to a higher level to include society.
sentences.zh: 然后在最近的新书中，我将模棱两可的失去理论提升到了一个更高的层面，将其延伸到了整个社会。

sentences.en: And globally, such as the pandemic, caused ambiguous losses for everyone on this world.
sentences.zh: 在全球范围内，例如大流行，给这个世界上的每个人都带来了模棱两可的失去。

sentences.en: And then it made me think about racism here because I live very near to where George Floyd was killed here in Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 这让我开始思考这里的种族主义，因为我住得离明尼阿波利斯乔治·弗洛伊德遇害的地方非常近。

sentences.en: And my eyes were opened with that videotape that that young woman took, Ardella Fraser.
sentences.zh: 年轻女性阿尔黛拉·弗雷泽拍摄的那段视频开阔了我的眼界。

sentences.en: And for some reason, it opened my thinking in a way that should have been opened before, but wasn't.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，它以一种本该早点打开、却一直没有打开的方式启发了我的思考。

sentences.en: Perhaps because we were locked in at the time, we were more reflective.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为我们当时被隔离在家，我们进行了更多的反思。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定是什么原因。

sentences.en: But at any rate, I believe that a cross-generational transmission of trauma from slavery
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，我认为跨代传递的奴隶制创伤

sentences.en: started with the ambiguous loss of slavery when families were torn apart on the auction block, sold off parents, one from the other, and parents from children.
sentences.zh: 始于奴隶制那模棱两可的失去，当时家庭在拍卖台上面临骨肉分离，父母被互相卖掉，父母与孩子被强行拆散。

sentences.en: And that that heinous crime of slavery has, in fact, not gone away.
sentences.zh: 而奴隶制那种滔天罪行，事实上并没有消失。

sentences.en: That is still the stress and the trauma of it is still with us today.
sentences.zh: 它所带来的压力和创伤直到今天依然伴随着我们。

sentences.en: And then I also mentioned more as a proposition for other people to study and not me.
sentences.zh: 然后我还顺便提出了一个供其他人而不是我来研究的命题。

sentences.en: I propose that climate change is causing ambiguous losses, the loss of clean water, the loss of fertile lands, the loss of a life as we knew it.
sentences.zh: 我提出气候变化正在导致模棱两可的失去，干净水源的失去、肥沃土地的失去、我们所熟悉的生活方式的失去。

sentences.en: And that will be for future generations to teSt.
sentences.zh: 这将由未来的世代去检验。

sentences.en: We actually did a podcast not long ago about climate change in which we talked to a couple of experts who discussed ecological grief.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我们实际上做了一期关于气候变化的播客，在节目中我们与几位专家探讨了生态悲伤。

sentences.en: And I think that's kind of what you're talking about, that you're grieving losses due to what's happening to our environment.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是你所谈论的，你在为环境变化所带来的失去感到悲伤。

sentences.en: How is that connected to the same feelings that we have with respect to, say, the pandemic or racism?
sentences.zh: 这与我们在面对大流行或种族主义时产生的感受有何联系？

sentences.en: Well, again, it's a loss you can't see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，同样地，这是一种你看不到的失去。

sentences.en: When someone dies, at least in normal times, we'd have a funeral, we'd have a ritual, there'd be a notice in the paper, there would be a death certificate,
sentences.zh: 当有人去世时，至少在正常时期，我们会举行葬礼，会有仪式，报纸上会有讣告，会有死亡证明，

sentences.en: there would be certainty about a loss with death.
sentences.zh: 对于死亡带来的失去会有确定性。

sentences.en: But there's also some other losses that have certainty, such as loss of money during the
sentences.zh: 但也有一些其他的失去是具有确定性的，比如新冠期间金钱的失去、新冠期间退休储蓄的失去、

sentences.en: COVID, loss of your retirement savings during COVID, loss of your house during COVID.
sentences.zh: 新冠期间房屋的失去。

sentences.en: Those all can be quantified.
sentences.zh: 这些都可以被量化。

sentences.en: But I'm talking about losses that have no quantification.
sentences.zh: 但我谈论的是那些无法量化的失去。

sentences.en: They are so uncertain, they're so unclear, that in fact, we don't list them, or we list them as deaths, as they did in the Civil War and in other wars.
sentences.zh: 它们是如此不确定，如此模糊，以至于事实上我们没有把它们列入统计，或者像在南北战争和其他战争中那样，把它们归类为死亡。

sentences.en: They are different, because the family has no assurance of death.
sentences.zh: 它们是不同的，因为家庭无法得到死亡的确切保证。

sentences.en: And now and then, a few people came walking out of the jungle.
sentences.zh: 然而偶尔会有人从丛林中走出来。

sentences.en: Or after 9-11 in New York, a few people were found in psychiatric institutions without remembering what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 或者在纽约9·11事件后，有一些人在精神病院被找到，却记不清发生了什么。

sentences.en: What makes this different is that we have all these ambiguous losses that have happened to us.
sentences.zh: 这其中的不同之处在于，我们身上发生了所有这些模棱两可的失去。

sentences.en: And so, the general population is talking about mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 因此，大众都在谈论心理健康问题。

sentences.en: Come on, there's stress issues.
sentences.zh: 拜托，这是压力问题。

sentences.en: And we're causing, we're calling too much a mental health problem that needs psychiatric help or psychological help.
sentences.zh: 我们把太多需要精神科帮助或心理帮助的情况称之为心理健康问题。

sentences.en: We're pathologizing a normal reaction to an abnormal situation.
sentences.zh: 我们将对异常情况的正常反应病理化了。

sentences.en: I'm going to repeat that.
sentences.zh: 我要重复一遍。

sentences.en: We cannot pathologize normal reactions to a pathological situation.
sentences.zh: 我们不能将对病态环境的正常反应病理化。

sentences.en: We have just had two years of a pathological situation.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚经历了为期两年的病态环境。

sentences.en: Literally, a pathogen out there where we can't see it, causing many, many deaths, many, many
sentences.zh: 字面意义上讲，一种我们看不见的病原体存在于世，造成了非常多的死亡，非常多的

sentences.en: illnesses, and just uprooting the entire world from what we used to do and how we used to live.
sentences.zh: 疾病，并彻底颠覆了全世界原本的生活方式和生活习惯。

sentences.en: We have had major loss, but not all the loss was quantifiable.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了巨大的失去，但并非所有的失去都是可量化的。

sentences.en: Yet, it is real.
sentences.zh: 然而，它是真实存在的。

sentences.en: So, I completely understand the ambiguity of the pandemic and what's been happening to us
sentences.zh: 所以，我完全理解大流行的模糊性以及过去两年里发生在我们身上的事情，但当有人去世时，甚至如果是一只宠物死去，我的意思是，那某种程度上是一个终点。

sentences.en: over the last two years, but when somebody dies, or even if a pet dies, I mean, that's sort of an end point.
sentences.zh: 难道这不正是我们应该觉得一切都结束了的事情吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that something where we should feel like it's done?
sentences.zh: 为什么那仍然是一种模棱两可的失去？

sentences.en: Why is that still an ambiguous loss?
sentences.zh: 为什么那仍然是一个模棱两可的损失？

sentences.en: It feels different to me qualitatively than the other things that you were just talking about.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这与你刚才谈论的其他事情在性质上有所不同。

sentences.en: It may be somewhat different, but there is no end point.
sentences.zh: 它可能确实有些不同，但并没有终点。

sentences.en: That is, there's a transformation from breathing to not breathing, from life to death.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，存在着从呼吸到停止呼吸、从生到死的转变。

sentences.en: That's a transformation.
sentences.zh: 那是一种转变。

sentences.en: And there is no closure on the relationship you had with that person or that pet.
sentences.zh: 而且，你与那个人或那只宠物之间的关系并没有真正的了结。

sentences.en: Indeed, something has changed, and we need to recognize that.
sentences.zh: 的确，有些事情已经改变了，我们需要认识到这一点。

sentences.en: But we'll recognize it more likely if people can differentiate between the physical ending, that is, the breathing ends, versus the attachment.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们能够区分物理上的终结（即呼吸停止）与情感上的依恋，我们就会更有可能认识到这一点。

sentences.en: So, I'm really coming out of attachment theory of Volby, which says that once you make an attachment
sentences.zh: 所以，我实际上是基于沃尔比的依恋理论，该理论指出，一旦你产生了某种依恋

sentences.en: to someone or something, I couldn't even talk about someone's home, you make an attachment
sentences.zh: 对某人或某物——我甚至可以说对某人的家，你都会产生一种依恋

sentences.en: that even if that thing is no longer with you, if the person has stopped breathing, or if you've lost that home or that pet, you can still feel attached to them.
sentences.zh: 即使那个事物不再陪伴着你，如果那个人已经停止呼吸，或者你失去了那个家或那只宠物，你依然会觉得与他们保持着依恋。

sentences.en: You can still say, I love that.
sentences.zh: 你仍然会说，我爱那个东西。

sentences.en: That was my favorite place.
sentences.zh: 那是我的最爱。

sentences.en: That was my, I love that person.
sentences.zh: 那是我的，我爱那个人。

sentences.en: That was my favorite pet of all times.
sentences.zh: 那是我有生以来最喜欢的宠物。

sentences.en: I love that pet.
sentences.zh: 我爱那只宠物。

sentences.en: I miss them.
sentences.zh: 我很想念他们。

sentences.en: But you know they're gone.
sentences.zh: 但你知道他们已经走了。

sentences.en: And so, we call that continuing bonds.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们称之为“持续的羁绊”。

sentences.en: It came first from the edited book by Klass, K-L-A-S-S, and other, his colleagues, that continuing bonds is what is normal grief.
sentences.zh: 这个概念最早源于克拉斯（K-L-A-S-S）及其同事合编的一本书，他们提出持续的羁绊才是正常的悲伤。

sentences.en: Getting over it is an artificial idea put upon, I think, of the people who are grieving in a culture that has no patience for suffering.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在这样一个对苦难缺乏耐心的文化中，要求人们“走出来”是一种强加在悲伤者身上的勉强观念。

sentences.en: We might be that culture.
sentences.zh: 我们可能就是这样的文化。

sentences.en: So, you wrote in your book about your own experience of loss from your early childhood memories of
sentences.zh: 所以，你在书里写到了自己早年对失落的亲身经历：

sentences.en: your immigrant father missing his Swiss homeland, your brother dying of polio as a child, and to your becoming a caretaker for your husband before he died in 2020.
sentences.zh: 你的移民父亲思念瑞士故土，你的弟弟在童年因小儿麻痹症夭折，以及你在2020年丈夫去世前照顾他的经历。

sentences.en: How have these personal experiences shaped how you think about loss today?
sentences.zh: 这些个人经历是如何塑造你今天对失落的看法的？

sentences.en: From the beginning, and the earliest loss was my little brother who died of polio the summer before the SOC vaccine came out.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，我最早经历的失落就是我的小弟弟，他在索尔克疫苗问世前的那年夏天死于小儿麻痹症。

sentences.en: My view already back then was that I didn't have to get over it.
sentences.zh: 当时我的看法就已经定型了，我觉得我不需要“走出来”。

sentences.en: But then I was a bit of a rebel right then already.
sentences.zh: 但那时候我其实就已经有点叛逆了。

sentences.en: But I lived in a Swiss immigrant community, New Glarus, Wisconsin, where everybody came from, in that case, Switzerland, they were all homesick.
sentences.zh: 不过我生活在一个瑞士移民社区——威斯康星州的新格拉鲁斯，那里每个人都来自瑞士（就这个例子而言），他们都有很重的乡愁。

sentences.en: I lived in an environment of homesickness in the village, but also in my home.
sentences.zh: 我不仅在村里，也在家庭中生活在一种弥漫着乡愁的环境里。

sentences.en: So, I was kind of accustomed to the fact that you don't cut bonds, you remember them, even though I had the sad version of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我某种程度上已经习惯了这样一件事：你不会切断羁绊，你会铭记他们，尽管我经历的是其中比较悲伤的版本。

sentences.en: A little heavy on the sadness side, I thought.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，悲伤的成分确实有点重。

sentences.en: But therefore, the community, I think, was perhaps advanced at that time in this regard, in that nobody ever told me I should get over it.
sentences.zh: 但正因如此，我认为当时的社区在这个问题上或许比较开明，因为从来没有人对我说过我应该“走出来”。

sentences.en: There was always remembering.
sentences.zh: 人们总是在怀念。

sentences.en: Class reunions would remember my dead brother, his classmates.
sentences.zh: 同学聚会时，我弟弟的同学们会缅怀他。

sentences.en: And so, I perhaps was lucky to live in an environment, as I was growing up, where there was no closure.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在成长过程中可能很幸运，生活在一个没有强求“了结”的环境里。

sentences.en: You remembered people every Memorial Day.
sentences.zh: 每逢阵亡将士纪念日，大家都会纪念故人。

sentences.en: You went to the grave sites and remembered them, and so on.
sentences.zh: 你会去墓地缅怀他们，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Today, it's a different story, as I live in a more urban environment now.
sentences.zh: 而现在情况不同了，因为我如今生活在更具都市化色彩的环境中。

sentences.en: And corporate ideas that, you know, will give you a week, three days, maybe, to grieve and then come back and be productive.
sentences.zh: 还有那些企业文化——你知道的，他们会给你一周甚至三天时间去悲伤，然后就得回来继续高效工作。

sentences.en: That assumes you get over it.
sentences.zh: 这种做法的前提是假设你已经“走出来”了。

sentences.en: And the thing is, you don't need to get over it.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，你根本不需要走出来。

sentences.en: Even with a clear-cut death, with a death certificate, with funeral after, and all the appropriate rituals, you don't need to get over it.
sentences.zh: 即使面对一场再清晰不过的死亡，有死亡证明，有随后的葬礼，以及所有相应的仪式，你也不需要走出来。

sentences.en: You can live with grief, and that's recommended.
sentences.zh: 你可以带着悲伤生活，这才是被建议的做法。

sentences.en: And Bonanno and other researchers say, and Neymar say, there's oscillation, that it ebbs and flows.
sentences.zh: 博南诺和其他研究人员，还有内马尔都指出，人是会摇摆的，悲伤会有起伏涨落。

sentences.en: Grief ebbs and flows, or comes in and out.
sentences.zh: 悲伤会起伏涨落，或进或退。

sentences.en: And over time, those ebbs and flows, oscillations, will be farther apart.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这些起伏涨落和心理摇摆的间隔会越来越长。

sentences.en: But they're never gone.
sentences.zh: 但它们永远不会消失。

sentences.en: There's never closure.
sentences.zh: 永远没有所谓的“彻底了结”。

sentences.en: So the latest research certainly is in the idea of living with loss, not getting over it.
sentences.zh: 因此，最新的研究无疑支持这样一种观点：与失落共存，而不是从失落中走出来。

sentences.en: And then in the book, I write about the fact that Freud, in fact, gave us a different message in his personal letters to his friends than he did in his academic writings.
sentences.zh: 我在书中还写到，弗洛伊德实际上在写给朋友的私人信件中表达的信息，与他在学术著作中表达的并不一样。

sentences.en: Because when the client said to him, I'm sorry about your daughter, who died.
sentences.zh: 因为当有人对他说：“听到你女儿去世的消息，我很难过”时

sentences.en: She died of the flu in 1920.
sentences.zh: 她是在1920年死于流感的。

sentences.en: And he said, no, she's still here.
sentences.zh: 他说：“不，她依然在这里。”

sentences.en: And he patted his vest pocket, wherein he must have had some memento of her.
sentences.zh: 然后他轻拍了拍背心口袋，里面一定装着她的某种纪念物。

sentences.en: Now, he never told us that in his academic writings.
sentences.zh: 然而，他在学术著作中从未提及过这一点。

sentences.en: He talked about detachment, and I talk about more Kubler-Ross and others, who write one way academically and write another way personally.
sentences.zh: 他谈论的是情感疏离，而我所谈论的库布勒-罗斯及其他人，则是学术上写一套，私底下又是另一套。

sentences.en: Kubler-Ross, in the end of her life, after she had nine strokes, many strokes, excuse me, but lived for nine years, not being able to walk.
sentences.zh: 库布勒-罗斯在生命的晚年——在经历了九次中风（抱歉，是多次中风）但依然带着无法行走的身体生活了九年之后

sentences.en: She said that dying was not the five stages which she meant them to be, that it wasn't linear, that it's messy.
sentences.zh: 她说过，临终并不像她原本所指的那样分为五个阶段，它不是线性的，而是杂乱无章的。

sentences.en: And it was messy for her, and she was angry about it a lot.
sentences.zh: 对她而言确实一团糟，为此她曾感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: So we need to take another look at our historical sages who changed their minds in their personal writings.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要重新审视我们那些在私人书信中改变了看法的历史先贤。

sentences.en: And I wrote this book more personally because I wanted to make sure I was congruent personally and professionally as much as I could.
sentences.zh: 我写这本书时带有更多个人色彩，因为我想确保自己在个人层面和专业层面上尽可能保持一致。

sentences.en: That's admirable.
sentences.zh: 这真令人钦佩。

sentences.en: I appreciate you telling that story.
sentences.zh: 我很感激你分享这个故事。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: For many younger Americans, the pandemic was their first experience for existential threat and a communal, large-scale loss.
sentences.zh: 对许多年轻的美国人来说，这场大流行是他们首次体验到生存威胁和群体性、大规模的失落。

sentences.en: Now, earlier generations lived through a major depression, world wars.
sentences.zh: 而过去的几代人曾经历过大萧条和世界大战。

sentences.en: People used to experience much more loss a lot earlier in life.
sentences.zh: 过去的人们在更年轻的时候就要经历多得多的生离死别。

sentences.en: Women commonly died in childbirth, or children died of communicable diseases that are no longer fatal because we have much better medicine and vaccines.
sentences.zh: 过去妇女死于分娩很常见，或者儿童死于那些如今不再致命的传染病，因为我们现在有了好得多的医药和疫苗。

sentences.en: But do you think that the pandemic has changed the way that the younger people today are thinking about risk, uncertainty, and loss?
sentences.zh: 但你认为，这场大流行是否改变了当今年轻人对风险、不确定性和失落的看法？

sentences.en: And do you think this will have lasting effects about how they approach loss and grief going forward?
sentences.zh: 你认为这会对他们未来的失落观和悲伤应对方式产生持久的影响吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: It's too soon to tell, but I predict there is going to be change as a result of this two years of turmoil and upheaval into our normal way of life.
sentences.zh: 现在下结论还为时尚早，但我预测，经历了两年的动荡和对我们正常生活方式的颠覆后，一定会产生改变。

sentences.en: In fact, we already see changes in how we do things, and I have great faith in young people for being resilient, more resilient than adults are, or the older we get.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们已经看到做事方式上的变化，我对年轻人保持韧性的能力抱有极大信心，他们比成年人或是年纪越大的人更具韧性。

sentences.en: And children are resilient, and children are resilient, and children are resilient too.
sentences.zh: 孩子们很有韧性，孩子们非常有韧性，孩子们也同样富有韧性。

sentences.en: They will remember this as I remembered the polio epidemic, as I remembered the depression, and as I remembered World War II as a child.
sentences.zh: 他们会记住这一切，就像我小时候记住小儿麻痹症大流行、大萧条以及第二次世界大战那样。

sentences.en: I was afraid by watching my parents' faces, I would know how afraid to be.
sentences.zh: 我当时会通过观察父母的脸来感到害怕，从而知道自己该有多害怕。

sentences.en: But in a way, what that taught us, and what we'll teach the young people now, I think, is that you can't always have your way.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，这给我们带来的启示——我认为也将教给现在的年轻人——就是你不可能事事顺心。

sentences.en: You can't always have the world be the way you want it to be.
sentences.zh: 世界不可能总是按你期望的那样运转。

sentences.en: There are tragedies.
sentences.zh: 生活中总会有悲剧。

sentences.en: There are difficult times.
sentences.zh: 总会有艰难的时期。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: We can get through them.
sentences.zh: 我们能够挺过去。

sentences.en: And I think what young people today may learn is that they got through this okay.
sentences.zh: 我想今天的年轻人可能会学到的一点是，他们成功挺过了这一切。

sentences.en: I talked to quite a few of them who missed college graduations, who were cut off from friends immediately without saying bye, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我和不少年轻人聊过，他们错过了大学毕业典礼，在没有来得及道别的情况下突然与朋友隔绝，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But they have a philosophic response to it that I find very mature.
sentences.zh: 但他们对此有一种哲学式的回应，我觉得非常成熟。

sentences.en: They found other ways to say goodbye to friends they couldn't say goodbye to in reality.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了其他方式，去向那些在现实中无法告别的朋友们说再见。

sentences.en: That they know they will have probably the best class reunions any of us have ever had down the line.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，在未来他们可能会迎来我们所有人有生以来最棒的同学聚会。

sentences.en: They got stronger because of it.
sentences.zh: 他们因此变得更坚强了。

sentences.en: And perhaps this generation I'm talking about, this is the first thing when things didn't go right for them, for many of them.
sentences.zh: 也许我所说的这一代人，对他们中的许多人来说，这是他们人生中第一次遇到事情没有按预期发展的情况。

sentences.en: Of course, there were exceptions.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有例外。

sentences.en: I realize that.
sentences.zh: 这一点我明白。

sentences.en: But we've had a parenting style for a while that I believe has interfered with the stress management development of the young people,
sentences.zh: 但一段时间以来，我们的某种育儿方式，我认为已经干预了年轻人压力管理能力的发展，

sentences.en: whereby parents would make sure their kids weren't distressed.
sentences.zh: 在这种方式下，父母会确保孩子们免受任何痛苦或困扰。

sentences.en: Well, being stressed and being able to cope with it teaches you that you are stronger than you think.
sentences.zh: 然而，感受到压力并能够应对压力，会向你证明你比自己想象的要坚强。

sentences.en: And that's a very valuable lesson for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 这对于你余下的人生来说是非常宝贵的一课。

sentences.en: And I can see that in many of the young people now.
sentences.zh: 我现在能在许多年轻人身上看到这一点。

sentences.en: They will be stronger for it.
sentences.zh: 他们会因此变得更坚强。

sentences.en: Not that I wish this on anyone.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我希望任何人经历这些。

sentences.en: But once adversity happens and you were resilient in it, you bent like a tree in a storm, but you got up again.
sentences.zh: 但一旦逆境降临而你展现出了韧性，像暴风雨中的大树一样弯曲却又重新挺立起来

sentences.en: You are stronger psychologically for having been through that.
sentences.zh: 经历过这一切后，你的心理会变得更加坚强。

sentences.en: So after writing and observing so much about grief and loss during your career, do you consider yourself basically an optimist or a pessimist about the human condition?
sentences.zh: 那么在你的职业生涯中，在写作和观察了如此之多的悲伤与失落之后，你认为自己本质上是对人类命运抱持乐观态度还是悲观态度？

sentences.en: Oh, I'm an optimiSt.
sentences.zh: 哦，我是个乐天派！

sentences.en: And I don't consider myself a grief expert because there's so many of them.
sentences.zh: 我不认为自己是什么悲伤专家，因为这类专家实在太多了。

sentences.en: I consider myself an expert on loss and the nuances of loss, the different kinds of loss, and the stress it causes.
sentences.zh: 我认为自己是关于失落、失落的细微差别、不同类型的失落以及由此带来的压力的专家。

sentences.en: I started out in the stress field, and that's essentially where I come from.
sentences.zh: 我最初从事的是压力领域的研究，这基本上就是我的专业背景。

sentences.en: Ambiguous loss is not a medical model focused on pathology.
sentences.zh: 模棱两可的失落（Ambiguous loss）并不是一个聚焦于病理学的医疗模型。

sentences.en: It's a stress model focused on resilience.
sentences.zh: 它是一个聚焦于韧性的压力模型。

sentences.en: As a result of that, and having come from a family of hard times during the Depression, and then, as I said, World War II, and seeing people, you know, stand up after that.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，由于我出身于一个在大萧条时期经历过艰难困苦的家庭，然后，正如我所说，经历过二战，并看到人们在经历这些后重新站立起来

sentences.en: And these were terrible things, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这些都是可怕的经历。

sentences.en: And now with the pandemic, again, I see people in a way that they have more maturity than I've ever seen before, in the young people especially.
sentences.zh: 而现在面对大流行病，我再次看到人们表现出前所未有的成熟，尤其是在年轻人身上。

sentences.en: And in other people, they've coped in very creative ways.
sentences.zh: 在其他人身上也是如此，他们以极具创造力的方式进行了应对。

sentences.en: Indeed, some have not, because some people believe in binary thinking.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些人并没有做到，因为有些人笃信二元思维。

sentences.en: And, of course, the science of the pandemic, science is never binary.
sentences.zh: 然而，关于大流行病的科学，科学从来都不是二元的。

sentences.en: It's always based on probability.
sentences.zh: 它永远是基于概率的。

sentences.en: And they wanted a clean answer.
sentences.zh: 而这些人想要一个明确的答案。

sentences.en: They wanted closure.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一个了断。

sentences.en: Am I in danger or not?
sentences.zh: 我到底有没有危险？

sentences.en: Do I wear a mask or do I not?
sentences.zh: 我该不该戴口罩？

sentences.en: Is the virus real or is it not?
sentences.zh: 病毒到底是真是假？

sentences.en: So, we saw a part of the population that needs absolute thinking, more like closure.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到一部分人群需要绝对化的思考，更倾向于寻找定论。

sentences.en: They think in binaries.
sentences.zh: 他们的思维是非黑即白的。

sentences.en: You know, you're either with me or you're not.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，要么跟我一路，要么就不是。

sentences.en: It's either dead or alive.
sentences.zh: 要么死，要么活。

sentences.en: It's either safe or it's not safe.
sentences.zh: 要么安全，要么不安全。

sentences.en: That way of thinking didn't work right now.
sentences.zh: 这种思维方式现在行不通了。

sentences.en: And these are not optimists, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这些人可不是乐天派。

sentences.en: So, I think if you can think in a more resilient way, if you can act in a more resilient way, flexible but learning from it, growing stronger each time,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，如果你能以更有韧性的方式思考，如果你能以更有韧性的方式行事——保持灵活但从中学习，每一次都变得更加坚强

sentences.en: you will also be optimistic because what that means is you can cope with most anything that comes along in life.
sentences.zh: 你也会变得乐观，因为这意味着你能够应对生活中遇到的几乎任何事情。

sentences.en: The death of your loved ones, accidents, loss of a job.
sentences.zh: 亲人的离世、意外、失业。

sentences.en: I don't wish that on anyone.
sentences.zh: 我并不希望任何人遭遇这些。

sentences.en: But, by the way, death is inevitable if only it's your parents getting older and eventually dying.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，死亡是不可避免的，哪怕只是你的父母日渐苍老并最终离去。

sentences.en: And so, life will bring its losses.
sentences.zh: 因此，生活总会带来它的失落。

sentences.en: And our practice with being resilient will pay off.
sentences.zh: 而我们培养韧性的练习将会带来回报。

sentences.en: It will let us know, as I wrote in the book, you can be knocked down, but you can get up again.
sentences.zh: 正如我在书中所写的那样，它会让我们明白：你可能会被打倒，但你能够再次站起来。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Boss, I think that's a wonderful message of hope.
sentences.zh: 好的，博斯博士，我认为这是一个充满希望的美妙讯息。

sentences.en: I appreciate your bringing it to our listeners today.
sentences.zh: 感谢你今天把它带给我们的听众。

sentences.en: I hope that they have learned some things that will help them through these trying times, which I think have been difficult for many of us.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们学到了一些东西，能够帮助他们度过这些对我们许多人来说都十分艰难的考验时期。

sentences.en: So, thank you for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常感谢你今天做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 不客气，我的荣幸。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 上，或者在 Apple、Stitcher 以及任何你获取播客的平台上找到往期的《心理学讲话》节目。

sentences.en: And if you listen on Apple, please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果你在 Apple 上收听，请给我们留下评价。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 地址是 speakingofpsychology，全部连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学讲话》由李·韦纳曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬（Chris Kondayan）。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是吉姆·米尔斯（Kim Mills），代表美国心理学会向您问候。
